sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS NRN-CNTRL NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS CNTRL PLAINS/MIDDLE MO VALLEY... UPPER RIDGE ACROSS MUCH OF THE CNTRL AND ERN U.S. WILL DEAMPLIFY TODAY AS A STRONG BELT OF WLY/S PERMEATE MUCH OF THE NRN TIER OF STATES IN RESPONSE TO A SERIES OF UPPER TROUGHS PROGRESSING EWD N OF THE U.S./CANADIAN BORDER. MOST NOTABLE UPPER FEATURE WILL BE A DISTURBANCE--CONVECTIVELY MODIFIED--AND EMBEDDED ON THE SRN FRINGE OF THE MANITOBA/WRN ONTARIO UPPER TROUGH...THAT WILL MOVE QUICKLY EWD FROM ERN ONTARIO TO THE ST. LAWRENCE SEAWAY BY MIDDAY AND THEN TO THE CANADIAN MARITIMES BY FRIDAY MORNING. ANOTHER MID-LEVEL PERTURBATION WILL DRIFT EWD FROM THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS TO THE CORNBELT AHEAD OF ANOTHER DIGGING SPEED MAX IN THE PACIFIC NW. IN THE LOW LEVELS...A COLD FRONT IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH AFFECTING NRN NEW ENGLAND WILL PUSH EWD THROUGH THIS REGION DURING THE AFTERNOON/EVENING HOURS. THIS BOUNDARY WILL PROBABLY BE MODULATED TO A CERTAIN EXTENT BY ONGOING CLUSTER/MCS ACROSS ONTARIO/QUEBEC THAT MAY PERSIST AND POSSIBLY SERVE AS AN EFFECTIVE IMPETUS FOR SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT FOR NEW ENGLAND. TRAILING PORTION OF THIS BOUNDARY WILL EXTEND WWD THROUGH THE SRN GREAT LAKES INTO THE CNTRL HIGH

sections.title: NRN-CNTRL NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: DETERMINISTIC MODELS INDICATE THAT STRONG SURFACE HEATING...ALONG WITH INCREASING LOW LEVEL MOISTURE...FED BY A PLUME OF UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S DEWPOINTS...AND A PIECE OF THE CNTRL U.S. EML WILL PROBABLY YIELD 1000-2500 J/KG MLCAPE BY EARLY-MID AFTERNOON. SOME UNCERTAINTY EXISTS REGARDING THE DEGREE OF DESTABILIZATION WITH FARTHER N EXTENT DUE PRIMARILY TO THE EVOLUTION OF ANY MCS THAT MOVES INTO THE REGION FROM CANADA BY LATE MORNING-EARLY AFTERNOON. REGARDLESS...IT APPEARS MORE THAN ADEQUATE INSTABILITY SHOULD DEVELOP DUE TO INCREASING LOW LEVEL MOISTURE FROM THE SW-W GIVEN APPRECIABLE LOWER TO MID-LEVEL FLOW ASSOCIATED WITH THE APPROACHING SHORTWAVE TROUGH. INCREASING SHEAR PROFILES ACROSS THE REGION WILL STRONGLY FAVOR ORGANIZED STORMS --INCLUDING SUPERCELLS/FORWARD PROPAGATING SYSTEM WITH BOWING SEGMENTS-- AND MAY BE CONDUCIVE FOR A CORRIDOR OF DMGG WINDS...ESPECIALLY IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE SURFACE LOW /I.E. NRN 2/3RDS MAINE/. MODEL GUIDANCE INDICATES THAT THE SURFACE LOW WILL UNDERGO SUBSTANTIAL DEEPENING THROUGH THE AFTERNOON HOURS--WITH ISALLOBARIC FORCING/RELATIVE BACKING OF LOW LEVEL WINDS AND A 50 KT LLJ ENLARGING LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPHS /300+ M2/S2 EFFECTIVE SRH/. sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS/MIDDLE MO VALLEY
sections.text: WITH THE AID OF A MODERATE/VEERING LOW LEVEL JET IN VICINITY OF A SURFACE FRONT ZONE...ONE OR MORE TSTMS CLUSTERS ARE FORECAST TO BE ONGOING EARLY THURSDAY MORNING ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE CNTRL PLAINS. DEBRIS CLOUD COVER MAY HINDER DESTABILIZATION WHILE OTHERWISE EFFECTIVELY SHIFTING THE FRONT SOUTHWARD...BUT IT SEEMS PROBABLE THAT MODERATE DESTABILIZATION WILL OCCUR NEAR THE FRONT WHERE LOW LEVEL MOISTURE WILL BE GREATEST. ALTHOUGH DEEP LAYER FLOW WILL BE MODEST...VEERING WINDS MAY SUPPORT SOME STORM ORGANIZATION IN THE FORM OF MULTICELLULAR CLUSTERS/TRANSIENT SUPERCELL STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF WIND DMGG/SOME HAIL AND PERHAPS A BRIEF TORNADO. THIS ACTIVITY MAY GROW UPSCALE INTO A MCS ACROSS ERN NEB/NERN KS INTO WRN IA AS THE LLJ REINVIGORATES BY THE LATE EVENING. FARTHER WEST...OTHER ISOLATED SEVERE TSTMS WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS THURSDAY AFTERNOON/EVENING VIA A POST-FRONTAL UPSLOPE REGIME.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST STATES/CAROLINAS
sections.text: VERTICAL SHEAR/LAPSE RATES ALOFT WILL BE VERY WEAK/POOR...BUT A SEASONABLY MOIST/UNSTABLE AIRMASS MAY SUPPORT A SPORADIC THREAT FOR POCKETS OF ISOLD WIND DMGG FROM WET MICROBURSTS DURING THE AFTERNOON HOURS. ..SMITH/KERR/COHEN.. 07/21/2011

sections.title: LOWER GREAT LAKES/NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED VORTICITY MAXIMUM WILL CONTINUE EWD TODAY THROUGH SRN QUEBEC AND MAINE IN TANDEM WITH 50 KT LOW- AND MIDLEVEL WIND MAXIMA. ASSOCIATED SURFACE LOW OVER SWRN QUEBEC WILL CONCURRENTLY DEVELOP ENEWD TO THE GULF OF ST. LAWRENCE BY TONIGHT WHILE TRAILING COLD FRONT PUSHES SEWD INTO NEW ENGLAND AND THE LOWER GREAT LAKES REGION. THE LEADING EDGE OF TSTM ACTIVITY ASSOCIATED WITH ABOVE-MENTIONED VORTICITY MAXIMUM HAS PROGRESSED MUCH MORE QUICKLY EWD THAN MODEL FORECASTS WITH THIS ACTIVITY OVERSPREADING PORTIONS OF NRN/CNTRL MAINE LATER THIS MORNING INTO AFTERNOON. ISOLATED OCCURRENCES OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS...THOUGH THE LIMITED DESTABILIZATION WILL LIKELY PRECLUDE A GREATER SEVERE WEATHER RISK WITH THIS INITIAL WAVE OF TSTMS. MORE ROBUST TSTM DEVELOPMENT IS ANTICIPATED THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING IN THE WAKE OF THE INITIAL STORMS AND INVOF MIDLEVEL IMPULSE AND ASSOCIATED SURFACE FRONT. HERE...STEEPING MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ATOP A MOISTENING BOUNDARY LAYER WILL YIELD MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING TO 1000-2000 J/KG. WHEN COUPLED WITH THE STRENGTHENING WLY/WSWLY DEEP-LAYER WIND FIELD...ENVIRONMENT WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS AND BOWING

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS/MID MO VALLEY
sections.text: NOCTURNAL MCS HAS GENERATED A COLD POOL...THE LEADING EDGE OF WHICH HAS PUSHED INTO S-CNTRL IA...NWRN MO TO ALONG THE NEB/KS BORDER. WHILE WEAK VORTICITY MAXIMUM LIFTING NEWD FROM NWRN KS/SWRN NEB MAY MAINTAIN TSTMS THROUGH THE MORNING ACROSS PORTIONS OF NEB/IA...DEEPENING LEE CYCLONE OVER ERN WY AND DEVELOPING THERMAL LOW OVER N-CNTRL KS/S-CNTRL NEB SHOULD SUPPORT A NET NWD MOVEMENT OF AGGREGATE SURFACE BAROCLINIC ZONE LATER TODAY. TO THE S OF THIS BOUNDARY...STRONG DAYTIME HEATING...BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S/LOW 70S AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL YIELD AFTERNOON MLCAPE OF 1500-3000 J/KG. THE RE-DEVELOPMENT OF SURFACE-BASED TSTMS IS EXPECTED LATER THIS AFTERNOON ALONG AGGREGATE BOUNDARY...PERHAPS AIDED BY ANOTHER WEAK IMPULSE EMANATING FROM THE CNTRL ROCKIES. FORECAST WIND PROFILES EXHIBIT VEERING WINDS WITH HEIGHT WITH AROUND 30 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR...SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED MULTICELL AND SOME SUPERCELL STRUCTURES WITH THE PRIMARY HAZARD BEING DAMAGING WINDS. ...CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS INTO CNTRL GULF COAST STATES AND TN VALLEY... WEAK VORTICITY MAXIMA ROTATING AROUND ERN/SRN PERIPHERY OF MIDLEVEL CYCLONE WILL SERVE TO FOCUS DIURNAL TSTM ACTIVITY ONCE AGAIN TODAY.

sections.title: NRN NEW ENGLAND TODAY
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER QUEBEC AND AN ACCOMPANYING SURFACE CYCLONE/COLD FRONT WILL PROGRESS EWD OVER THE SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY AND NRN NEW ENGLAND BY THIS EVENING. A CLUSTER OF THUNDERSTORMS IN ADVANCE OF THE WAVE IS NOW APPROACHING MAINE FROM SE QUEBEC...AND THESE STORMS WILL LIKELY OVERSPREAD THE NRN HALF OF MAINE DURING THE AFTERNOON. FARTHER SW...ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON ALONG THE TRAILING COLD FRONT ACROSS THE NRN VT/NH AREA. THE BIGGEST CONCERNS AT THIS TIME ARE THE DEGREE OF ADDITIONAL DESTABILIZATION ACROSS MAINE GIVEN THE INCREASING CLOUDS...AND THE COVERAGE OF STORMS FARTHER SW INTO NY/NRN NEW ENGLAND GIVEN ONLY SUBTLE FOCI FOR INITIATION S OF THE PRIMARY SHORTWAVE TROUGH PATH. VERTICAL SHEAR IN THE WARM SECTOR WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS AND EMBEDDED BOW ECHOES...WITH EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT AND EFFECTIVE SRH IN EXCESS OF 200 M2/S2. DEBRIS CLOUDINESS AND RAIN WILL LIMIT SURFACE HEATING ACROSS THE NRN THIRD OF MAINE...WITH LESSER IMPACTS ACROSS NRN VT/NH. STILL...THE NERN EXTENT OF THE LOW 70S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS ACROSS WRY NY/ONTARIO WILL SPREAD ENEWD AND CONTRIBUTE TO DESTABILIZATION. THE NET RESULT WILL BE AN E

sections.title: IA/NEB/KS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: THE OVERNIGHT CONVECTION IS WEAKENING ACROSS ERN NEB/IA...THOUGH SUBSTANTIAL DEBRIS CLOUDS WILL LIKELY PERSIST INTO THE AFTERNOON. OUTFLOW FROM THE MORNING STORMS HAS REINFORCED THE COLD FRONT WHICH NOW EXTENDS FROM SE IA ACROSS NW MO TO N CENTRAL KS. THE FRONT SHOULD STALL SOON...AND MAY EVEN RETREAT A LITTLE TO THE N THIS AFTERNOON IN RESPONSE TO HIGH PLAINS LEE CYCLOGENESIS. MEANWHILE...STRONG SURFACE HEATING ALONG THE FRONT WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 2000-3000 J/KG. ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORM IS EXPECTED BY LATE AFTERNOON ALONG THE FRONT AS CONVECTIVE INHIBITION WEAKENS...AND ASCENT IS LOCALLY ENHANCED BY A REMNANT MCV MOVING ENEWD OVER NEB. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR NEAR 30-40 KT COULD SUPPORT A FEW ORGANIZED CLUSTERS/MARGINAL SUPERCELL STORMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. FARTHER W...ISOLATED STORMS COULD POSE A MARGINAL SEVERE RISK IN THE WEAK UPSLOPE REGIME FROM E/NE CO TO SW SD.

sections.title: SE STATES/TN VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: THUNDERSTORM POTENTIAL THIS AFTERNOON WILL BE DRIVEN BY MESOSCALE PROCESSES LIKE DIFFERENTIAL HEATING AROUND THE FRINGES OF THE MORNING MS/AL CONVECTION...AND NEW DEVELOPMENT WITH THE REMNANT CLUSTER/COLD POOL ACROSS TN/KY. STEEPENING LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND MODERATE INSTABILITY COULD SUPPORT A FEW STORMS WITH STRONG DOWNBURST WINDS THIS AFTERNOON...THOUGH COVERAGE SHOULD REMAIN ISOLATED. ..THOMPSON/BOTHWELL.. 07/21/2011
